name: email-send
description: Send a new email. to and cc take a contact ID, or "principal" for the principal; you choose the person and the address comes from their verified identities. A #label (principal#personal, or on each cc entry) is a hint for which labelled identity, not an address. Emails are sent from the agent's configured email address. Pass account only together with reply_to_message_id, to read and send a threaded reply from that mailbox. A new email always goes from the primary account.

inputs.to: string (contact ID or "principal", optional #label hint such as principal#personal — a hint, not an address. Not a contact yet: contact-create first)
inputs.cc: string? (comma-separated contact IDs or "principal", each with an optional #label hint such as the contact ID plus #work — a hint, not an address)
inputs.subject: string
inputs.account: string? (named account to thread a reply from, as configured under Settings → Channels → Email → Email accounts — the Account line on the inbound email preamble. Only valid together with reply_to_message_id — the quoted original is read from this account and the reply is sent from it. Omit it, and do not pass it on a new email, to use the primary account.)
inputs.reply_to_message_id: string? (Nylas message ID — when set, the original message is quoted below the reply and the send is threaded)
inputs.attachments: object[]? (file attachments — array of {file_url: string, filename: string, content_type: string, node_id?: string}. file_url must be a file:// URL from email-download-attachment, drive-download-file (for a Drive file — use it, not get_drive_file_content, which is text-only and not binary-safe), or similar. When the attachment contains KG-sourced data, set node_id to the kg_nodes UUID so export gates can resolve sensitivity. Max 10 attachments, 20 MB total.)
inputs.export_items: object[]? (parallel to attachments — array of {node_id: string, label: string} tagging each attachment's KG source for bulk-export gates. Required when sending confidential+ attachments; one entry per attachment in the same order. Pass it, or node_id on each attachment, whenever an attachment carries KG-sourced data (facts, documents, downloaded reports): without node IDs the gate treats every item as internal, so confidential thresholds never fire.)
inputs.context_bridge: string? (JSON — optional context bridge registration that adds a delegation hint so the agent can route any reply faster. Tracking is automatic but best-effort even without it: registration happens after the send and can fail, and what it registers expires — unless you set expires_in_hours, about 3 days on email, the same with or without this parameter (on a task-wake turn, about 7 days). Invalid JSON, a non-object, or no agent_id drops the whole bridge, delegation hint included, without telling you. An invalid optional field (e.g. an expires_in_hours that is not a positive number) is dropped on its own, also without telling you, and the rest of the bridge still registers. A valid expires_in_hours replaces that default outright, in either direction: a smaller number gives a shorter window, not a longer one (a deployment may configure a different default). Set expires_in_hours whenever the reply may land after that — a request routed through an organisation's process rather than a person, an ask sent before a holiday or a long trip, anything a slow answer is normal for. Err on the longer side: a stale entry costs a little noise, while an expired one loses the thread. If the entry expired or was never registered, the reply arrives as an unrecognised cold inbound. Shape: {agent_id, expected_reply?, delegation_hint?, metadata?, expires_in_hours?}. delegation_hint must be the agent id of the specialist that owns the reply (e.g. calendar); a hint naming no registered specialist is dropped. Example: {"agent_id":"coordinator","delegation_hint":"calendar","expected_reply":"confirmation or reschedule request"})

outputs.to_identity: string? (label of the address used for a reference to, or "primary" or "unlabelled")
outputs.cc_identities: string[]? (one per distinct cc address, in that order; repeated references are omitted)
outputs.subject: string
